reasoning: Within the last 45 days, I was unable to locate any Indiana-specific general-election polling for the 2026 Senate race or for a future presidential contest; the only fresh electoral data were for a U.S. House district and national generic ballot, which cannot be treated as direct measures of a statewide Senate or presidential margin.[1][10] Structurally, Indiana remains a clearly Republican-leaning state, with the latest Cook Partisan Voting Index indicating a statewide tilt of roughly R+9, and 2024 presidential results showing Donald Trump winning the state by about 19 points, reinforcing the GOP advantage.[9][11] Given the absence of race-specific statewide polling in the last 45 days, the best current quantitative indicator of statewide partisan lean is this structural R+9 PVI figure, rather than a true up-to-date Senate or presidential polling margin.
